name: 柳家榨房
The Liu Press House
before: 林子里一座老榨房，房梁上横着一根粗大的榨杆，杆头吊着一块黑沉沉的铁疙瘩当坠子，是柳三娘她爹留下的。一伙骑手冲进榨房，要拆了榨杆当柴，铁坠子拿去换钱。三娘拿着酒勺堵在门口：「这房子你们拆，坠子不许碰。我爹说过，那坠子不是我家的。」

An old press house in the woods, a massive press beam across the rafters with a lump of black iron hung from its end as a weight, left by Liu Sanniang's father. A band of riders bursts in to break up the beam for firewood and sell the weight. Sanniang blocks the door with her ladle. 'Pull the house down if you like, but don't touch the weight. My father said it isn't ours.'
after: 骑手们跑了，大个子把铁坠子取了下来，拿袖子一擦，黑锈底下露出铜色和字：「千里号护卫都头」。三娘这才想起她爹临死前的话：那年千里号的都头拿它押在柳家，存下三百坛酒，「人回来，凭令开坛」。她爹怕人偷，就挂在榨杆上，「压在最重的地方，谁也拿不走」。都头在王城三年，教过一营禁军，带出来的老兵都认这块令。拿到兵营宣一声「都头回来了」，他们就来投。三娘说：「酒我替他们守着，令你们拿去，叫人。」

The riders flee and the giant takes down the iron weight. One wipe of his sleeve and under the black rust shows bronze, and characters: 'Qianli caravan. Captain of the escort.' Only now does Sanniang remember her father's dying words: that year the caravan's escort captain pledged it to the Liu family and stored three hundred jars of wine. 'When the men come back, the token opens the jars.' Afraid of thieves, her father hung it on the press beam. 'Put it where the weight is heaviest and no one can take it.' In his three years at the King's city the captain trained a whole battalion of the guard, and the veterans he made all know this token. Read it out in a barracks, 'The Captain's back', and they'll come. Sanniang says: 'I'll keep the wine for them. Take the token and call the men.'

name: 柳家老窖
The Old Liu Cellar
before: 三娘要补的三坛酒，存在林中山坡下的老窖里。窖门大开，一伙国舅府的戟士正往外搬坛子，又往里搬坛子：搬出去的是柳家的好酒，搬进来的坛子一模一样，只在坛口拴了一根细细的红绳。三娘凑过去一闻，脸色变了：「这酒里下了东西。」

The three jars Sanniang needs are in the old cellar under a wooded slope. Its door stands wide open, and some of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers are carrying jars out and carrying jars in: out go the Liu family's good wines, in come jars exactly like them, but with a fine red string tied round each neck. Sanniang leans in to sniff and her face changes. 'There's something in this wine.'
after: 戟士们跑了，红绳坛子一个个砸碎在沟里。窖的最里头整整齐齐码着三百坛，坛口封泥上都压着「千」字，十年了没人动过。三娘从自家的存酒里补足了三坛，对那三百坛只鞠了个躬：「人家存的，动不得。」大个子在墙上刻：红绳酒，是要在春宴上给宫里喝的。

The halberdiers flee and the red-string jars are smashed in the gully one by one. At the back of the cellar stand three hundred jars in neat rows, each clay seal stamped 'Qian', untouched for ten years. Sanniang makes up her three jars from the family's own stock and simply bows to the three hundred. 'Somebody else's. Not to be touched.' The giant carves on the wall: the red-string wine was meant for the palace to drink at the spring banquet.

name: 题坛亭
The Jar-Label Pavilion
before: 林中小亭里关着一个落第秀才，专给酒坛写签，字写得漂亮，城里的酒坊都找他。黄家雇的弓手把他看在亭子里，逼他给黄家的酒写广告，他写一条，弓手念一条，念完都说不够响亮。秀才写到第三十条，已经写出了「喝黄家酒，长生不老，娶妻十房」。

In a small pavilion in the woods a failed scholar is kept prisoner. He writes labels for wine jars in a beautiful hand, and every winery in the city wants him. The archers hired by the Huang family guard him in the pavilion and force him to write advertisements for Huang wine. He writes one, the archers read it out, and every time they say it isn't loud enough. By the thirtieth he's written: 'Drink Huang wine: live for ever and take ten wives.'
after: 弓手们跑了，秀才把三十条广告揉成一团扔进了湖里。他说柳家的王单他也写过签，可宫里有个怪规矩：二百九十九坛，坛坛贴签，签上不许写字。「宫里自己写，」他说，「我问写什么，收酒的人说，写名字。」

The archers flee, and the scholar crumples all thirty advertisements into a ball and throws it in the lake. He's written labels for the Liu family's royal order too, he says, but the palace has an odd rule: two hundred and ninety-nine jars, a label on every jar, and nothing written on any label. 'The palace writes them itself. I asked what, and the wine receiver said: names.'

name: 黄家酒栈
The Huang Wine Depot
before: 野地里一座大酒栈，挂着「黄」字招牌，是黄家酒坊在路上的货栈，弓手守在门楼上。栈里囤着成垛的酒坛，可坛里装的多半是兑了水的酸酒。三娘隔着墙闻了闻，啐了一口：「这也配叫酒？」

A large wine depot in the open country under a 'HUANG' signboard: the Huang winery's roadside storehouse, archers on its gate tower. Inside are stacks of jars, most of them sour wine cut with water. Sanniang sniffs over the wall and spits. 'Call that wine?'
after: 弓手们跑了，酒栈里的酸酒全倒进了沟里，沟里的青蛙叫了一夜。三娘把栈里的空坛子都收了，说明年装好酒，「坛子是无辜的」。

The archers flee and the sour wine all goes into the ditch, where the frogs croak all night. Sanniang collects every empty jar in the depot to fill with good wine next year. 'The jars aren't to blame.'
first: 酒栈里抄出八坛没兑水的陈酿（黄家留着自己喝的）、两车葡萄干、一筐核桃、三十张新羊皮，还有一本黄家给国舅府的账：「春宴红绳酒，一百坛」。

The depot gives up eight jars of undiluted old wine (kept for the Huangs' own table), two carts of raisins, a basket of walnuts, thirty new sheepskins, and a Huang account to the Royal Uncle's house: 'Red-string wine for the spring banquet: one hundred jars.'
pass: 每次路过，在栈里改行搬坛子的摘葡萄汉子们都给你们灌满水囊，囊里不是水，是新榨的葡萄汁，甜得粘嘴：「三娘说的，赶路的人不喝酒。」

Every time you pass, the grape pickers who now haul jars at the depot fill your waterskins, not with water but with fresh-pressed grape juice so sweet it sticks to your lips. 'Sanniang's orders. Travellers don't drink wine.'

name: 鳄苇荡
Crocodile Reeds
before: 酒驼队要过湖北角的一片苇荡，苇子比骆驼还高，水下趴着一群大鳄，最大的那条有两丈长，背上的鳞像一排瓦。它们夜里上岸晒肚皮，白天藏在苇根里，听见驼铃就往水边游。三娘说每年送酒都要在这里折几峰骆驼，「它们认得驼铃」。

The wine caravan must cross a reed marsh at the lake's northern corner, reeds taller than camels and a pack of great crocodiles lurking beneath the water, the biggest two fathoms long with scales on its back like a row of roof tiles. At night they haul out to bask; by day they hide among the reed roots, and at the sound of camel bells they swim for the edge. Sanniang loses a camel or two here every year. 'They know the bells.'
after: 大鳄们被赶回了湖心，驼队一峰不少地过了苇荡。可岸边的泥里埋着一窝窝鳄蛋，太阳一晒，明年又是一群小鳄；绿洲的大鳄一年年孵下去，杀不尽，只能隔一阵来清一回，让过湖的人走得安稳些。

The great crocodiles are driven back to the middle of the lake and the caravan crosses the reeds without losing a camel. But clutches of eggs lie buried in the mud along the shore, and with the sun on them there'll be a new brood next year. The oasis crocodiles hatch year after year and can't be wiped out; all you can do is come back every so often and clear them, so those crossing the lake can go in peace.

name: 湖北石市
North Shore Stone Market
before: 湖北岸的林子里有个石市，山里采来的青石在这里凿成磨盘、井圈、封坛石，换外头运来的铁器。如今石市冷冷清清：国舅府的戟士守着市口，说铁器归府里专卖，石匠不许私换。石匠们没铁凿，只好拿石头敲石头。一个白胡子老石匠坐在一堆小圆石中间，每块石头上都凿了个坑，正好扣住坛口。

In the woods on the lake's north shore lies a stone market, where bluestone quarried in the hills is cut into millstones, well rings and jar seals and traded for ironware from outside. Now it's deserted: the Royal Uncle's halberdiers hold the entrance and say iron is a House monopoly; masons may not trade for it privately. With no iron chisels, the masons are reduced to knocking stone with stone. A white-bearded old mason sits among heaps of small round stones, each hollowed to fit over the mouth of a jar.
after: 戟士们走了，铁器一车车拉进来，石料一车车拉出去，石市又响起了叮叮当当。老石匠是给宫里春酒凿封坛石的，凿了六年。他翻出六年前头一回的单子给你们看：「封坛石三百枚」，「三百」被一笔划掉，旁边改成「二百九十九」，下面一行小字：「前数误，多算了一个。」老石匠说：「王的单子，就错过这一回。」三娘看着那行字，半天没说话。

The halberdiers leave, iron comes in by the cartload and stone goes out by the cartload, and the market rings with chisels again. The old mason has cut the seals for the palace's spring wine for six years. He digs out the very first order from six years ago: 'Jar seals: three hundred'. 'Three hundred' is struck through with a single stroke and corrected to 'two hundred and ninety-nine', and below, a line in small writing: 'Previous figure in error. Counted one too many.' 'The only time a King's order was ever wrong,' says the old mason. Sanniang looks at that line and says nothing for a long while.

name: 截北道
The North Road Barricade
before: 去王城北门的大路上横着三道鹿砦，国舅府的人马三路排开：戟士守鹿砦，弓手上了路边的土台，铁骑在两头堵着。路口竖着一块牌子：「春酒禁入。」后头一行小字是新添的：「柳家的尤其不许。」三娘看了，把酒勺往腰里一别：「那就看看谁不许。」

Three rows of abatis bar the high road to the city's north gate, the Royal Uncle's forces in three ranks: halberdiers holding the barricades, archers on earthen platforms by the road, cavalry blocking either end. A sign stands at the entrance: 'No spring wine to enter.' Below it, freshly added in small characters: 'Especially not the Liu family's.' Sanniang reads it and tucks her ladle into her belt. 'Let's see who says so.'
after: 鹿砦被推倒，国舅府的人马退回了城里。驼队爬上一道坡，王城的北墙就在眼前，墙根下有几个冒着凉气的小孔，三娘说那是宫里酒窖的气眼，「酒到了窖里，冬暖夏凉，跟人一样，要喘气」。

The barricades go down and the Royal Uncle's forces fall back into the city. The caravan climbs a rise, and there before you is the city's north wall, a few small holes breathing cool air at its foot. Those are the vents of the palace wine cellar, says Sanniang. 'Wine in a cellar keeps warm in winter and cool in summer, and like a man, it has to breathe.'

name: 验数台
The Counting Platform
before: 北门外有一座土台，每年春酒到了，宫里的收酒官就站在台上验数，数三遍，才放进城。今年台上站的却是一队陌生的弓手，说收酒官「告病了」，由他们来收，收了直接送去国舅府。三娘一眼就看穿了：「收酒官的嗓子我听了六年，你们谁都不是。」

Outside the north gate is an earthen platform where every spring the palace's wine receiver stands to check the count, three times over, before letting the wine into the city. This year a squad of strange archers stands there instead, saying the receiver has 'fallen ill' and they'll take delivery, straight to the Royal Uncle's house. Sanniang sees through them at once. 'I've heard the receiver's voice for six years. None of you is him.'
after: 假收酒的跑了，真收酒官被人从台底下的草棚里放了出来，一个结结巴巴的老头。他站上台，一坛一坛数了三遍：二百九十九，不多不少。他说每年交完酒回宫，王都要问他一句：「今年路上，有没有人回来？」他说没有。「王就说：那就再存一年。」

The fake receivers flee, and the real one is let out of a straw shed beneath the platform: a stammering old man. He climbs up and counts jar by jar, three times: two hundred and ninety-nine, no more, no less. Every year when he reports back to the palace, he says, the King asks him one thing: 'This year on the road, has anyone come back?' And he says no. 'Then the King says: keep it another year.'

name: 红绳林
Red-String Wood
before: 湖东的林子里有一处废猎苑，黄家的老掌柜就躲在这里，身边护着一队国舅府的戟士。红绳酒的事露了，他准备连夜逃走，车上装着一箱金子和一百根没用完的红绳。三娘追到林子边，冷笑一声：「我爹说过，卖酒的人往酒里下东西，下辈子做酒糟。」

In the woods east of the lake lies a disused hunting park, where the old master of the Huang winery is hiding under the guard of a squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers. With the red-string wine found out, he's preparing to flee overnight, a chest of gold and a hundred unused red strings on his cart. Sanniang chases him to the edge of the wood and gives a cold laugh. 'My father said: a wine seller who doctors his wine comes back next life as the dregs.'
after: 戟士们跑了，黄掌柜被捆在车上，老老实实招了：红绳酒里下的是蒙汗药，国舅要在春宴上让宫里的人睡上一夜，「趁王睡着，取王的印」。他还说国舅最近见了一伙戴金面具的人，「说是从千佛洞来的，要的是金子」。

The halberdiers flee, and Master Huang, roped to his own cart, confesses meekly: the red-string wine is drugged, and the Royal Uncle means to put the palace to sleep for a night at the spring banquet. 'While the King sleeps, take the King's seal.' He adds that the Royal Uncle recently met a band of men in golden masks. 'Said they came from the Thousand Buddha Caves. What they want is gold.'

name: 高跷门
The Stilt Gate
before: 北门城墙上站满了国舅府的弓手，城门半掩，谁的车进门都要翻个底朝天。三娘的驼队排在门外进不去，那伙被她雇来的高跷艺人凑过来出主意：他们踩着高跷，在城门前演一出「八仙过湖」，弓手们一看热闹，酒就从侧门溜进去。

The north wall is lined with the Royal Uncle's archers and the gate stands half closed, every cart turned upside down before it's let through. Sanniang's caravan is stuck outside the gate. Up come the stilt acrobats she hired with an idea: they'll perform 'The Eight Immortals Cross the Lake' on stilts in front of the gate, and while the archers gawp the wine can slip in by the side door.
after: 戏演到一半，弓手们看出了门道，可已经晚了：你们冲上了城墙，高跷艺人一边打一边还在唱。二百九十九坛酒从侧门进了城，一滴没洒。领头的艺人从高跷上探下身来，冲三娘一抱拳：「工钱照算，再加一坛！」三娘说：「这里的一坛都不能动，回去给你们开。」

Halfway through the show the archers twig it, but too late: you're already up on the wall, and the acrobats keep singing as they fight. All two hundred and ninety-nine jars go in by the side door without a drop spilt. The leading acrobat leans down from his stilts and salutes Sanniang. 'Wages as agreed, plus a jar!' Sanniang says: 'Not one of these jars can be touched. I'll open one for you back home.'

name: 老藤园
The Old Vine Garden
before: 北门外剩下最后一片葡萄园，园里一棵老藤爬满了半亩架子，主人白老藤和他的藤一样老。黄家买走了周围所有的园子，只剩他这一片死活不卖，黄家就派弓手守在园门口，谁来买葡萄、买葡萄干，就射谁的筐。今年的葡萄干堆在棚子里，堆得发了霉。

Outside the north gate lies the last vineyard, one ancient vine spread over half an acre of trellis, its owner Old Vine Bai as old as his vine. The Huang family bought up every garden around, but he flatly refused to sell, so they posted archers at his gate to shoot the basket of anyone who came to buy grapes or raisins. This year's raisins lie heaped in the shed, going mouldy.
after: 弓手们跑了，白老藤把发霉的挑出去，好的装了一车又一车，要跟你们换东西，价钱让了三成：「谢你们护着三娘的酒。」他说那棵老藤，是千里号的人当年帮他嫁接的，「他们说，藤活着，人就回得来」。每年秋天，宫里都派人来买这棵藤上的头一串葡萄。

The archers gone, Old Vine Bai sorts out the mouldy raisins and loads the good ones cart after cart to trade with you, thirty per cent off. 'Thanks for guarding Sanniang's wine.' That old vine, he says, the Qianli people helped him graft. 'They said while the vine lives, the men can come home.' Every autumn the palace sends someone to buy the first bunch of grapes from it.

name: 王窖口
The King's Cellar
before: 宫墙北角一道石阶通向地下，是王的酒窖。窖口被一队国舅府的戟士占了，说春酒既然进了城，就由国舅府「代收」。三娘的二百九十九坛堆在阶前，收酒官急得直结巴：「窖，窖里，王，王不许外人进！」戟士们已经开始往窖里搬自家的空坛子了。

A flight of stone steps at the north corner of the palace wall leads underground: the King's wine cellar. A squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers has seized the entrance, saying that since the spring wine is in the city, the House will 'receive it on the King's behalf'. Sanniang's two hundred and ninety-nine jars stand at the foot of the steps, and the receiver is stammering in alarm: 'The c-cellar, the K-King allows no outsider in!' The halberdiers have already started carrying their own empty jars down.
after: 戟士们被赶了出去。窖里一排排码着六年的春酒，一坛没开，每坛贴着一张签，签上一个名字：赵满仓、孟小山、老周……一年二百九十九个，年年一样。案上放着今年的空签、一支笔、一方砚，墨还是湿的。三娘把新酒一坛坛放好，轻声说：「这些人，都还没回来喝。」

The halberdiers are thrown out. Inside, row on row, stand six years of spring wine, not one jar opened, each with a label bearing a single name: Zhao Mancang, Meng Xiaoshan, Old Zhou... Two hundred and ninety-nine a year, the same every year. On the table lie this year's blank labels, a brush and an inkstone, the ink still wet. Sanniang sets the new wine in place jar by jar and says softly: 'None of these men has come back to drink yet.'

name: 搁船坡
Beached-Boat Slope
before: 离湖还有十几里的一道干坡上，搁着一条大木船，船底垫着滚木，船舱里炊烟袅袅，住着一家子。国舅府的一队弓手围着船，要拆船板去修府里的凉亭。船老大姓胡，一家五口全趴在船舷上，把锅碗瓢盆往下扔，扔得弓手们抱头乱跑。

On a dry slope more than ten li from the lake sits a great wooden boat, rollers under its hull and cooking smoke curling from the cabin: a family lives aboard. A squad of the Royal Uncle's archers has surrounded it to strip its planks for a pavilion at the House. The boatmaster, Old Hu, and his family of five are all leaning over the gunwale pelting them with pots and pans, sending the archers running with their arms over their heads.
after: 弓手们跑了。胡老大说这船从他爷爷那辈起就在湖上，可湖自己会走：他这辈子拿滚木拖着船追了四回湖，「湖往哪儿挪，我就往哪儿拖」。如今湖又往东南挪了，他得再拖一回。坡上一圈圈白色的螺壳，就是湖以前的岸。

The archers flee. This boat has been on the lake since his grandfather's day, says Old Hu, but the lake moves of its own accord: four times in his life he's dragged the boat on rollers to chase it. 'Wherever the lake shifts, I drag.' Now it's moved south-east again and he must drag once more. The rings of white snail shells up the slope are the lake's old shores.

name: 滚木道
The Roller Road
before: 胡老大的船要从这片野地上拖过去，路上却扎着一座国舅府的大营，戟士、弓手、铁骑都有，把附近所有能当滚木的树都砍了，堆在营里当柴烧。胡老大说国舅府放了话：湖往哪里走，归国舅府定，「谁私拖船，就是偷湖」。

Old Hu's boat must be dragged across this stretch of open country, but a large camp of the Royal Uncle's sits in the way, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, having cut down every tree nearby that could serve as a roller and stacked them in camp as firewood. The Royal Uncle's house has decreed, says Old Hu, that where the lake goes is for the House to decide. 'Drag a boat without leave and you're stealing the lake.'
after: 大营被冲开，滚木都抢了回来，胡家五口喊着号子把船往前拖，一天拖了三里。夜里胡老大指着地上的裂纹给你们看：一道道盐白的纹路，「湖走过的地方，就留下盐」。他说他从小就想知道湖为什么会走，「问了一辈子，没人说得清」。

The camp is broken, the rollers recovered, and the Hu family of five haul the boat forward to their own chant, three li in a day. At night Old Hu points out the cracks in the ground: white lines of salt. 'Wherever the lake's been, it leaves salt.' All his life he's wanted to know why the lake moves. 'Asked my whole life. Nobody could tell me.'

name: 湖祝坛
The Lake Priestess's Altar
before: 湖边林子里筑着一座土坛，坛上站着一个披白麻的女人，自称湖祝，带着一群信徒拦住过路人，把人家的水囊一只只夺过来，倒进湖里。她说湖在死，是因为人从湖里拿走了太多的水，「还给它，它就不走了」。信徒们拿弓守着路口，有个过路的老人渴得倒在坛下，她也不给一口。

An earthen altar stands in the lakeside woods, and on it a woman in white hemp who calls herself the Lake Priestess. With her followers she stops travellers, snatches their waterskins one by one and pours them into the lake. The lake is dying, she says, because people have taken too much of its water. 'Give it back, and it won't leave.' Her followers guard the road with bows. An old traveller has collapsed of thirst below the altar, and she won't give him a mouthful.
after: 信徒们散了，老人喝上了水。胡老大蹲下来对湖祝说：湖不是死，是走。湖靠河养着，上游的河一改道，湖就跟着河挪，老湖底晒成盐滩，新湖在河到的地方涨起来，「你倒一辈子水，也拦不住一条河」。湖祝坐在坛上，望着湖，一句话也没说。

The followers scatter, and the old man gets his water. Old Hu crouches and speaks to the priestess: the lake isn't dying, it's moving. A lake lives off its river, and when the river changes course upstream, the lake follows; the old bed dries in the sun into salt flats and a new lake rises wherever the river now reaches. 'Pour water all your life and you won't stop a river.' The priestess sits on her altar gazing at the lake and says not a word.

name: 改道石
The Course-Change Rock
before: 胡老大想亲眼看看河是在哪里改的道，领着你们往林子深处的一条干河床走。河床宽得能跑马，两岸的树根悬在半空，如今成了一伙走私客的暗道：他们骑着马，驮着私货，在干河床里来去，外头的人谁也看不见。见有人来，他们就在河床里拉开了阵势。

Old Hu wants to see with his own eyes where the river changed course, and leads you deep into the woods to a dry riverbed wide enough to gallop down, tree roots hanging in mid-air along its banks. It's become a smugglers' hidden road: mounted, their contraband on pack horses, they come and go along the riverbed unseen by anyone outside. When they see you coming, they form up across the bed.
after: 走私客被赶出了河床。河床拐弯的地方立着一块大石头，石头上刻着一行字，是从前守河的人留的：「丙午年夏，大水，河改道南去。」胡老大算了算：十一年前。「那年湖开始往南挪，城这边就旱了，」他说，「旱了整整三年，直到那三百个外乡人来。」

The smugglers are driven from the riverbed. At its bend stands a great rock with a line carved on it, left by the old river wardens: 'Summer of the Bingwu year. Great flood. The river changed course and went south.' Old Hu works it out: eleven years ago. 'That year the lake began to move south and this side of the city went dry,' he says. 'Three whole years of drought, until those three hundred outsiders came.'

name: 拦湖坝
The Lake-Turning Dam
before: 林子边上，国舅府抓了几百个民夫，要修一道大坝，「把湖拦回来」。坝修了三年，湖还是一年年往南挪，坝离湖越来越远，民夫们修的坝底下早就没水了。监工的戟士、弓手、铁骑三路守着，修慢了就抽鞭子。民夫们说，这坝是国舅亲自画的，「他说他不信湖会走」。

At the edge of the woods the Royal Uncle's house has rounded up hundreds of labourers to build a great dam 'to turn the lake back'. Three years they've been building it, and still the lake moves south year by year; the dam is ever further from the water, and there's been none at its foot for ages. Halberdiers, archers and cavalry stand over them in three ranks, whipping anyone who's slow. The Royal Uncle drew up the dam himself, the labourers say. 'He says he won't believe a lake can move.'
after: 监工的人跑了，民夫们扔了扁担回家。胡老大看着那道干坝直摇头：「湖拉不回来，只能跟着走，要不就像那三百个人那样，挖一条渠，把水引过来。」一个老民夫说，国舅的姐姐，就是老王后，死在旱的头一年，「从那以后，他见不得湖走」。

The overseers flee and the labourers drop their carrying poles and go home. Old Hu shakes his head at the dry dam. 'You can't drag a lake back. You can only follow it, or do what those three hundred did: dig a channel and bring the water to you.' An old labourer says the Royal Uncle's sister, the old Queen, died in the first year of the drought. 'Ever since, he can't bear to see the lake move.'

name: 万商营
The Merchants' Encampment
before: 王城南门外扎着一大片帐篷，波斯的、粟特的、回鹘的、吐蕃的商人挤在一起，有的已经住了半年，带来的货都快放坏了。国舅府的人马守着去南门的路：戟士堵路，弓手上了沙丘，铁骑来回巡，要进城，先交一成的货。商人们凑在一起骂，七八种话，骂的是同一句。

Outside the city's south gate sprawls a great encampment of tents, Persian, Sogdian, Uighur and Tibetan merchants crowded together, some of them here for half a year, their goods close to spoiling. The Royal Uncle's forces hold the road to the south gate: halberdiers blocking it, archers on the dunes, cavalry patrolling. To enter the city, first hand over a tenth of your goods. The merchants huddle and curse in seven or eight languages, all saying the same thing.
after: 国舅府的人马被赶回了城门口。商人们围着你们的旗子看了半天，一个粟特老商人说城里的万国商馆有十二根旗杆，十一根挂着各国的旗，第十二根空了十年，是留给中原朝廷的。「国舅要把那根杆子锯了，」他说，「王不许。王说杆子留着，旗会来。」

The Royal Uncle's forces are driven back to the gate. The merchants gather round your banner and look at it a long time. An old Sogdian says the Hall of Ten Thousand Nations in the city has twelve flagpoles: eleven fly the flags of the nations, and the twelfth has been bare ten years, kept for the court of the Central Plains. 'The Royal Uncle wants it sawn down,' he says. 'The King won't allow it. The King says keep the pole; the flag will come.'

name: 钦差渡
The Envoy's Landing
before: 河边的税关看见你们的旗子，关长连帽子都没戴正就跑了出来，一口咬定你们是朝廷微服私访的钦差。他摆了一桌全羊宴，席上塞来一盘金子，又塞来一个侄女，非要你们收下。你们说是商队，他不信，笑得更殷勤了：「懂，懂，钦差都这么说。」桌子底下，他的骑手们已经把刀拔出了半截。

At the sight of your banner, the riverside customs master comes running out with his hat on crooked, convinced you're the court's envoy travelling incognito. He lays on a whole roast sheep, pushes a plate of gold across the table, then a niece, insisting you accept. You say you're a caravan. He doesn't believe it and smiles all the harder. 'Of course, of course, every envoy says that.' Under the table his riders have their swords half drawn.
after: 关长的骑手们没收买成钦差，就想灭了口，结果被你们打下了河。关长跪在泥里递上账本，账上一笔笔全是替国舅府走的私货。等他听明白你们真是商队，当场晕了过去，醒来第一句是：「那金子，能还我吗？」

The customs master's riders, failing to buy the envoy, tried to silence him instead, and ended up knocked into the river. Kneeling in the mud the customs master hands over his ledger, every entry contraband run for the Royal Uncle's house. When he finally grasps that you really are a caravan, he faints on the spot. His first words on coming round: 'That gold. Can I have it back?'

name: 税关货仓
The Customs Warehouse
before: 税关后头有一座大货仓，是关长替国舅府扣下的货，各国商人的东西堆在一处：成匹的丝、成箱的胡椒、成捆的地毯，一队骑手守着仓门，钥匙挂在领头的脖子上，睡觉也不摘。

Behind the customs post stands a large warehouse holding goods the customs master has impounded for the Royal Uncle's house, every nation's merchandise in one heap: bolts of silk, crates of pepper, bales of carpets. A troop of riders guards the door, the key round their leader's neck. He doesn't take it off even to sleep.
after: 骑手们跑了，钥匙连着绳子被你们拽了下来。货仓的门打开，扣下的货一样样还给了万商营的商人们，各家认各家的，认完了，还剩下一堆没人认的：都是国舅府自己的私货。

The riders flee and you yank the key off, cord and all. The warehouse door opens, and the impounded goods go back one by one to the merchants of the encampment, each claiming his own. When they've finished, a pile remains that no one claims: the Royal Uncle's house's own contraband.
first: 没人认的那堆里抄出十匹蜀锦、三箱胡椒、两卷波斯地毯、一桶上好的灯油，还有一摞空白的「国舅府通关牒」，印都盖好了。

The unclaimed pile gives up ten bolts of Shu brocade, three crates of pepper, two rolls of Persian carpet, a barrel of fine lamp oil, and a stack of blank 'House of the Royal Uncle passes', already stamped.
pass: 每次路过，万商营的商人们都轮流请你们吃饭，今天波斯的抓饭，明天吐蕃的糌粑，后天回鹘的烤包子，吃完各塞一包干粮，谁也不肯落在后头。

Every time you pass, the merchants of the encampment take turns to feed you: Persian pilaf today, Tibetan tsampa tomorrow, Uighur baked dumplings the day after, and each presses a bundle of provisions on you afterwards. Nobody will be outdone.

name: 补旗铺
The Banner Mender's
before: 粟特老商人说，进万国商馆，旗得是新的，你们这面补了三块的可不行。南门外有个老裁缝专做旗子，可他的铺子被一队国舅府的戟士封了，铺里的黄绸红绸全被收走，说是「旗料归府」。老裁缝坐在门口，拿一根针在空中比画，比画的是一面谁也看不见的旗。

To enter the Hall of Ten Thousand Nations, says the old Sogdian, your flag must be new. That one with three patches won't do. Outside the south gate an old tailor makes banners, but his shop has been sealed by the Royal Uncle's halberdiers and every bolt of yellow and red silk taken, 'banner cloth belongs to the House'. The old tailor sits at his door sewing the air with a needle, stitching a flag no one can see.
after: 戟士们跑了，绸子要了回来。老裁缝拿起你们的旧旗看了很久，摸着那三块补丁，把新绸子放下了：「这面不换。补过三回的旗，才是走过路的旗。」他只把旗边的线头一根根收好，又在旗杆头缝了一圈红绸，「挂上去，看着精神」。

The halberdiers flee and the silk is recovered. The old tailor picks up your old banner and studies it a long time, fingering the three patches, then sets the new silk aside. 'Not this one. A flag that's been patched three times is a flag that's travelled.' He just tidies the loose threads along the edge one by one and sews a band of red silk round the head of the pole. 'Hang it up. It'll look smart.'

name: 南墙旗楼
South Wall Flag Tower
before: 南墙上一座破旗楼，住着万国商馆的老旗官，国舅说他「年老昏聩」，把他关在楼上，派了一队弓手守着楼梯。老旗官每天在楼窗前站一个时辰，望着城里商馆的方向。他腰上缠着一根长长的旗绳，粗得像手腕，他说那是第十二根杆子的绳。

On the south wall stands a dilapidated flag tower where the old flag officer of the Hall of Ten Thousand Nations lives. The Royal Uncle declared him 'senile' and shut him up there with a squad of archers guarding the stair. Every day the old officer stands an hour at the tower window, gazing towards the Hall in the city. Round his waist is wound a long halyard thick as a wrist. It's the rope from the twelfth pole, he says.
after: 弓手们跑了，老旗官下了楼，腰上的旗绳一圈圈解下来，足有十丈。他说国舅想在第十二根杆子上挂国舅府的旗，他就把绳子解下来缠在自己身上，「绳在我身上，谁也挂不上去」。一缠就是六年。他看着你们的旗：「来了就好，旧的也好。」

The archers flee and the old flag officer comes down, unwinding the halyard from his waist turn by turn, a good ten fathoms of it. The Royal Uncle wanted to fly his own house's flag on the twelfth pole, he says, so he took the rope down and wound it round himself. 'While the rope's on me, nobody can hoist anything.' He's worn it six years. He looks at your banner. 'It's come. That's what matters. Old is fine.'

name: 南门瓮城
The South Gate Barbican
before: 王城南门是一座瓮城，外门开着，内门关着，进了外门的人就被关在瓮城里，等着交钱。国舅府的人马守在城头和内门后：戟士、弓手、铁骑，三路都有。万商营的商人们跟在你们后头，老旗官扛着旗绳走在最前面，冲城头喊了一嗓子：「开门！朝廷的旗到了！」

The city's south gate is a barbican: the outer gate stands open, the inner gate shut, and whoever passes the outer gate is trapped inside to wait and pay. The Royal Uncle's forces hold the walls and the inner gate, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, all three. The merchants of the encampment follow behind you, and the old flag officer marches at the very front with the halyard over his shoulder, bellowing up at the wall: 'Open up! The court's flag is here!'
after: 内门被撞开了，商人们的驼队一溜进了城，驼铃响成一片，七八种话喊着同一句「到了」。城里的街上有人推开窗户往外看，看见那面打着补丁的旗，有个老太太叫出了声：「朝廷的人，又来了。」

The inner gate is battered open and the merchants' camel trains stream into the city, bells jangling, seven or eight languages shouting the same word: 'Here!' Along the streets people push open their windows to look, and at the sight of that patched banner an old woman cries out: 'The court's people. They've come again.'

name: 万国商馆
Hall of Ten Thousand Nations
before: 王城的河边一座大院，院门上刻着「万国商馆」四个字，院里立着十二根旗杆，十一根上的旗被风扯得哗哗响，第十二根光秃秃的，杆身上的漆却是新刷的。商馆被国舅府的一队铁骑占着，馆里各国的柜台全空着，他们宣布：商馆从今往后只做国舅府一家的生意，第十二根杆子明天就锯。

A great compound by the river in the King's city, 'HALL OF TEN THOUSAND NATIONS' carved over its gate. Twelve flagpoles stand in the courtyard: on eleven the flags snap in the wind, the twelfth is bare, yet its paint is fresh. A troop of the Royal Uncle's cavalry occupies the Hall, every nation's counter inside empty. From now on, they announce, the Hall trades with the Royal Uncle's house alone, and tomorrow the twelfth pole comes down.
after: 铁骑被赶出了商馆。老旗官把十丈旗绳穿进第十二根杆子的滑轮，你们的旗一点点升上去，补丁朝着太阳。各国的柜台一个个重新开张，西边的金子换东边的木料，账房的算盘噼啪响成一片。老旗官说杆子上的漆是王每年派人来刷的，十年没断过；王还留过一句话给第一个挂旗的人：「旗挂上了，账就该对了。」

The cavalry are thrown out of the Hall. The old flag officer threads his ten fathoms of halyard through the pulley of the twelfth pole and your banner climbs it bit by bit, patches to the sun. One by one the nations' counters open again, gold from the west trading for timber from the east, the clerks' abacuses clattering all at once. The paint on the pole, the old officer says, the King has sent someone to renew every year, ten years without a break. And the King left a message for the first to hoist a flag on it: 'When the flag is up, it's time the accounts were settled.'

name: 朝廷使馆
The Court Envoy's Residence
before: 荒野里一座带围墙的宅院，门楣上「朝廷使馆」四个字被泥糊住了一半。十年前朝廷的使臣住在这里，后来路断了，人走了，宅子被国舅封了，派了最精的一支人马守着，戟士守门，弓手上墙，铁骑在外头绕。老旗官说，宅子里还有一样东西，国舅一直想烧，王一直不许。

A walled residence out in the wilds, the words 'COURT ENVOY'S RESIDENCE' over its gate half plastered over with mud. Ten years ago the court's envoy lived here. Then the road was cut, the man left, and the Royal Uncle sealed the house and set his finest troops to guard it, halberdiers at the gate, archers on the walls, cavalry circling outside. There's still something inside, says the old flag officer, that the Royal Uncle has always wanted to burn and the King has never allowed.
after: 精兵退了。使馆的书房里落满了灰，案上压着一封朝廷八年前的来书：「问千里号下落。」底下是一封没寄出去的回书，墨色新旧不一，只有一句：「千里号之账，臣自当之。」老旗官说王从来不肯自称「孤」，「跟谁说话都是一个我字，写信给朝廷，倒写起臣来了」。

The picked troops fall back. The study is thick with dust, and on the desk lies a letter from the court eight years ago: 'Asking after the Qianli caravan.' Beneath it is a reply never sent, its ink of several ages, only one sentence long: 'The Qianli caravan's account, your servant will answer for himself.' The King never would call himself 'We', says the old flag officer. 'To anyone at all he just says I. And writing to the court, he puts your servant.'

name: 夜扯旗
The Night Raid on the Flag
before: 旗挂上的第一夜，一伙国舅府的人马摸到了商馆后墙下：戟士扛着梯子，弓手搭着火箭，铁骑在巷口接应，要把第十二根杆子上的旗烧了。各国商人被惊醒，拎着秤杆、算盘、量布的尺子从柜台后头冲了出来，谁也不比谁跑得慢。

The first night the flag is up, a party of the Royal Uncle's forces creeps up under the Hall's back wall: halberdiers with ladders, archers nocking fire arrows, cavalry waiting at the mouth of the lane, all to burn the flag on the twelfth pole. Woken by the noise, the merchants of every nation charge out from behind their counters with steelyard beams, abacuses and cloth measures, none slower than the next.
after: 国舅府的人被赶出了巷子，火箭全掉进了河里。天亮的时候，旗还在杆子上，只燎黑了一角。商人们轮流守夜，波斯珠宝商守上半夜，粟特老商人守下半夜。他们说：「这面旗挂着，我们的买卖就有人认。」

The Royal Uncle's men are chased out of the lane and every fire arrow ends up in the river. At dawn the flag is still on its pole, one corner singed black. The merchants take turns keeping watch, the Persian jeweller the first half of the night, the old Sogdian the second. 'While this flag flies,' they say, 'someone stands behind our trade.'

name: 十二灯楼
The Twelve-Lamp Tower
before: 南墙的转角有一座灯楼，楼顶十二盏灯，是万国商馆的老规矩：十二根杆子都挂了旗，十二盏灯就一起点，照得半个湖都亮。十年来只点过十一盏。今夜商人们想点第十二盏，楼梯口却守着一队国舅府的弓手，灯油被他们倒进了墙下的沟里。

At the corner of the south wall stands a lamp tower with twelve lamps on top. It's an old custom of the Hall of Ten Thousand Nations: when all twelve poles fly flags, all twelve lamps are lit together, bright enough to light half the lake. For ten years only eleven have burned. Tonight the merchants want to light the twelfth, but a squad of the Royal Uncle's archers holds the stair, and they've tipped the lamp oil into the ditch below the wall.
after: 弓手们跑了，商人们从各家柜台凑来了灯油，第十二盏灯点着了。十二盏灯一起亮起来的时候，湖面上一片金光。过了一会儿，王宫的方向也亮起了一盏灯，就一盏，亮了很久才灭。老旗官说：「王看见了。」

The archers flee, the merchants pool lamp oil from their counters, and the twelfth lamp is lit. When all twelve blaze together, the lake turns to gold. After a while a single lamp lights up in the direction of the palace, just one, and burns a long time before going out. 'The King has seen,' says the old flag officer.

name: 记债墙
The Debt Wall
before: 南墙里侧有一段老墙，墙砖上密密麻麻写满了粉笔字，是王城几十年的老规矩：谁欠谁的，写在墙上，全城作证；还清了，自己来擦。一队国舅府的戟士正拿石灰浆往墙上刷，刷得白花花一片：国舅府欠的债，都写在这面墙上。

On the inner face of the south wall runs an old stretch covered in chalk writing, a custom of the King's city for decades: who owes whom is written on the wall for the whole city to witness, and when it's paid, the debtor comes and wipes it off himself. A squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers is slapping lime wash over it, turning it blank white: the Royal Uncle's house's debts are all written on this wall.
after: 戟士们跑了，石灰还没干透，底下的字还能认。屋檐底下有一块砖，雨淋不着，石灰也没刷到，字是十年前的：「千里号欠王城水一车。」后面跟着另一个人的字，小一些：「以渠抵。尚欠一人。」那几个字一直没人来擦。

The halberdiers flee. The lime isn't yet dry and the writing beneath can still be read. Under the eaves is one brick the rain never reached and the lime missed, its writing ten years old: 'The Qianli caravan owes the King's city one cart of water.' After it, in another, smaller hand: 'Repaid with a channel. Still owing: one man.' Nobody has ever come to wipe those words off.

name: 拖船入河
Where the Boat Meets the River
before: 胡老大一家把船从野地一路拖到了王宫外的河边，船底的滚木都磨成了薄片。可河岸上守着一队国舅府的铁骑，说河归国舅府管，「这河上只许走国舅府的船」，要把胡家的船推回坡上。胡老大的小孙女站在船头，冲铁骑们吐了一口唾沫。

The Hu family has dragged their boat all the way from the open country to the river outside the palace, the rollers under the hull worn to slivers. But a troop of the Royal Uncle's cavalry holds the bank, saying the river belongs to the House. 'Only the House's boats may sail this river.' They mean to push the Hu boat back up the slope. Old Hu's little granddaughter stands at the bow and spits at them.
after: 铁骑被赶跑了。胡家五口一声号子，大船滑进了河里，船身一沉，又浮了起来，晃了两晃，稳了。胡老大说这回不是追湖，是等湖：「湖跟着河走，河在这儿，湖总有一天会来。」他说他要把船撑到王宫的水门下，「去看看那个不让锯旗杆的王」。

The cavalry driven off, the Hu family give one heave together and the boat slides into the river, sinks, bobs back up, rocks twice and steadies. This time, says Old Hu, he isn't chasing the lake but waiting for it. 'The lake follows the river. The river's here, so one day the lake will come.' He'll pole the boat to the palace water gate, he says, 'and take a look at the King who wouldn't let them saw down the flagpole'.
